findings.summary: The jump across the ledge gap is too demanding for the opening section. The player fell four times, questioned whether the jump was possible, and needed about 24 seconds of retries to cross.

quotes.text: Come on, that's way too far.

evidence.visual: The character runs along the opening green path, jumps towards the next small green platform, falls into the gap below, returns to the path and repeats the same jump several times before finally landing and continuing into the brown-walled area.

findings.suggested_fix: Move the landing platform about one tile closer to the take-off edge and make it twice as wide, so this opening jump can be made without a near-perfect run-up.

findings.summary: The objective says to reach a beacon, but no beacon or marker can be seen in the plaza. The player went in circles for most of the 40 seconds in this zone before finding the corner steps by chance.

quotes.text: I'm just going in circles here.

evidence.visual: No beacon is visible from ground level in the sandy plaza. The player loops among tall brown pillars and crates, checks walls and dead ends, passes the same places again, and only after about 30 seconds of wandering finds the small green-topped steps in a far corner and climbs them.

findings.suggested_fix: Add a tall, bright column of light over the raised exit reached by the corner steps, tall enough to be seen above the plaza pillars from the plaza entrance, and keep the objective wording as 'Reach the beacon'.

findings.summary: The player did not know how to open the gate. Nothing visibly linked the closed gate to the red button on the high shelf, so the player tried the gate itself and searched the room for about 29 seconds before spotting the button.

quotes.text: Is that a button up there?

evidence.visual: The player enters a checkered room with a closed wooden gate in the brown far wall, walks into the gate and tries to move it, circles the crates, and only at about 94 s looks up at the raised shelf. The player then climbs a crate to the shelf and stands on the red button, after which the gate opens.

findings.suggested_fix: Paint one thick red line on the wall and floor from the gate to the crate and up to the button shelf, and give the red button a steady pulsing glow, so the player can connect the gate with the button while still solving the crate climb.

findings.summary: An enemy is placed where the player lands from the drop, where it cannot be seen in advance. It killed the player twice almost immediately after landing before the player got past on the third attempt.

quotes.text: What? I couldn't even see it.
That's not fair. It gets you the second you land.

evidence.visual: The player drops down a narrow chute into a green-floored room where a red-spotted mushroom is waiting close to the landing and the exit doorway. The player is killed shortly after landing on the first two drops and only gets through on the third drop.

findings.suggested_fix: Move the mushroom's starting position to the far side of the drop room, several tiles away from the landing square, so the player lands safely, sees it, and has time to react.

findings.summary: The EXIT sign at the fork points the player into a dead end. The player trusted the sign, walked the left branch, hit the dead end and had to backtrack to the fork.

quotes.text: dead end but the sign said exit

evidence.visual: The player reaches a white EXIT sign with a red arrow pointing left, follows the left branch through the green-walled maze, reaches a dead end, turns around and retraces the route to the fork before taking the other branch towards the corridor.

findings.suggested_fix: Rotate the red arrow on this EXIT sign so it points along the branch that leads to the corridor instead of into the fork_left dead end.

findings.summary: The final corridor is a long, empty straight walk with nothing to do or decide. The player commented on how long it went on while walking its full length for about 40 seconds.

evidence.visual: For about 40 seconds the character simply walks straight down a long green corridor lined with repeated grey slabs, with no choice, obstacle or new sight, until the red flag on its yellow base finally appears near the end.

findings.suggested_fix: Cut the corridor to half its current length by removing the middle section of repeated slabs and reconnecting the entrance to the flag end, reducing the straight walk to about 20 seconds.
